# Theory

**Homophily**

Homophily is a concept that addresses the fact that "a contact between similar people occurs at a
higher rate than among dissimilar people" [@SNASS]. It thus is about if we share similar
characteristics, such as gender or ethnicity, we are more likely to befriend one another. Studies
show that this is also likely to occur on a socioeconomic level, and that students are more likely
to connect with students that have the same socio-economic status [@ZWIER2023127]. Socioeconomic
status is both about educational level and income-level, but this study solely looks at parental
educational level. In this study, the selection process that is expected to take place is that
students are expected to befriend other students whose parents have the same educational level, even
when controlling for gender and ethnicity. On a macro-level, I expect to see that the network is
segregated based on this characteristic, and on a micro-level, I expect that segregation is
especially taking place when looking at reciprocated ties, so whose friendships are *answered*.

*Hypothesis 1:* The MLC network is segregated on parental education level.

*Hypothesis 2:* Reciprocated ties are more likely to exist among students with parents with the same
educational level

**Redirected ties**

That person A sees person B as a friend, does not necessarily have to mean that person B sees person
A as a friend as well. However, one can imagine that if a friendship is answered, this creates more
social satisfaction than if ties are only sent, but not answered. Therefore, it is expected that:

*Hypothesis 3* Reciprocated ties positively affect students' social satisfaction

**Cultural values**

The family one grows up in influences the values one has and what world one is prepared for.
Stephens et al. (2014) show that there is a difference in how working class families and middle
class families prepare their children for the world, they, in fact, prepare their children for
different types of worlds. First generation students are often guided by more interdependent motives
than continuing-generation students and these norms remain the same over time in college
[@phillips2020]. Not having to navigate between different cultural contexts is likely to be less
demanding for students, therefore, it is expected that if students befriend people who have parents
with a similar educational level, they have probably similar expectations in terms of friendships
and it increases their social satisfaction.

*Hypothesis 4*: If reciprocated ties occur between students with parents with the same educational
level, this positively affects students' social satisfaction
